issues.description: ClaimReview JSON-LD in generate-html.js (line 1513) uses ${counts.total} (our WIN count, currently 72) in the "claimReviewed" field, where it should use ${context.domeClaimedConfirmed} (the dome's own claimed count, 69). This misrepresents what the dome claims: "The dome has 72 confirmed predictions" vs the correct "The dome claims 69 confirmed predictions." The ClaimReview schema is meant to represent the claim being reviewed (dome's own claim), not our entry count.

issues.title: WIN-010.c12 H1: geographic-magnetic latitude correlation across 9-station cohort not acknowledged
issues.description: WIN-010.c12 H1 (moderate): Geographic latitudes for 9 stations cluster in 30-50° band (COI 40.2°N, EBR 40.8°N, SPT 39.5°N, CLF 48.0°N, NGK 52.1°N, HAD 51.0°N, ESK 56.0°N, LER 60.1°N, HER 34.4°S) while magnetic latitudes differ. issues.description: WIN-008.c5 H1: Source attribution in detail_evidence says "Domain 16 in the live-power output (monitor.py) hardcodes..." — curmudgeon notes raw-text/08-live-power.txt shows "Domain 16: Telluric Cutoff (11.7 Hz)" but predicted=11.788 Hz and observed=11.7869 Hz appear to be in monitor.py itself, not in the live-power display name. WIN-043.c6 H2: detail_extra forward-falsification paragraph attributes 2024-2025 deceleration to "Livermore et al. 2020; Chulliat et al. 2020" but those papers discuss NMP dynamics through ~2020, not 2024-2025 acceleration. Attribution should either be dropped or use post-2022 data sources.

WIN-069.c7 H3 new: the "in absolute positional terms" qualifier added recently lacks a relative-error parallel for cross-WIN consistency with WIN-057. Should add a concise clause showing what the relative error is alongside the absolute positional error.

WIN-053.c12 H1 carry-forward: third charitable reading (i) sub-paragraph doesn't note that "the dome publishes no aperture-area ratio in its parameters; the only published signal is 5-pole monopole pair distance." Needs one-sentence tightening.

WIN-068.c16 H0: finding says Kim & Chang (2018) ensemble "predicts the 39-eclipse signal magnitude and geometry" — "predicts" is too strong; should be "reproduces" or "is consistent with". The paper is descriptive of the Sq mechanism, not a forward prediction.
